items.title: v2 items list with inStock=true returns only in-stock items and counts only them
covers: AC2: lists only products with at least one unit in stock
AC2: the product count counts only those
AC5: GET /api/catalog/items v2 accepts an optional in-stock filter
items.reason: The API filter is the source of truth for the WebApp list and its counts (AC2, AC5); if it filtered after counting, or not at all, the shopper would see out-of-stock products or a wrong total. Functional is the cheapest layer that runs the real query against Postgres.

items.title: Stock boundary: 1 unit is listed, 0 units is not
covers: AC2: at least one unit in stock (boundary 1 in, 0 out)
items.reason: AC2 sets the limit at "at least one unit"; an off-by-one (`>= 0` or `> 1`) would either show sold-out products or hide the last unit. Brand Daybird holds both sides of the limit (item 71 at 1, items 13, 53, 92 at 0), so one functional request checks just inside and just outside.

items.title: inStock=true filters before paging (type filter, second page)
covers: AC2: the pages count only in-stock products
AC3: paging keeps the filters
Impl notes: filter before counting and paging
items.reason: If the filter were applied after `Skip/Take`, a page would hold fewer than 9 items or skip in-stock items, and the total would not match the pages (AC2, AC3). Ski/boarding has 18 items, 4 of them out of stock, so the second page of 9 shows exactly whether paging runs on the filtered set.

items.title: inStock=true combines with brand and type filters
covers: AC3: in stock, brand and type apply at once
items.reason: AC3 requires all filters to apply together; a filter that replaced the brand or type condition instead of adding to it would return the wrong set. Daybird + Ski/boarding has 4 items, 2 of them out of stock, so each filter visibly removes items.

items.title: v2 items list without inStock is unchanged
covers: AC5: without the filter the list is exactly as today
items.reason: AC5 protects every existing client of the v2 list: without the new parameter, out-of-stock items must still be listed and counted. A default of `true` or a filter applied unconditionally would silently shrink the catalog for all callers.

items.title: v2 items list with inStock=false lists every item
covers: AC5: the in-stock filter is optional
Impl notes (product owner): when true, keep only in-stock items
items.reason: The product owner's note filters only "when true"; an explicit `false` means the filter is off and must not be read as "only out-of-stock" (a plausible inversion bug). Kept separate from TC-INSTK-1-05 because it exercises a different binding path (value present, not absent).

items.title: v1 items list ignores inStock
covers: AC5: the filter is added to version 2.0
Impl notes (product owner): version 1.0 does not change
items.reason: The filter belongs to version 2.0 only; version 1.0 clients must keep getting the full list even if they send the parameter. Sharing `GetAllItems` between versions makes leaking the filter into v1 an easy mistake.

items.title: OpenAPI v2 document describes inStock; v1 document does not
covers: AC5: the v2 list accepts an optional in-stock filter
Impl notes (product owner): describe it in the version 2.0 OpenAPI document; version 1.0 does not change
items.reason: API consumers discover the filter from the OpenAPI document; the product owner asked for it in v2 and for v1 to stay unchanged. Functional, because the document is generated by the running host (`/openapi/v{n}.json`), as the Ordering contract tests already read it.

items.title: Catalog shows an "In stock only" option, off by default
covers: AC1: an 'In stock only' option next to the Brand and Type filters, off by default
items.reason: AC1 is visible UI only: where the option sits and that it starts off. Only the WebApp on the test stack renders the filter panel, so this is e2e.

items.title: Turning "In stock only" on lists only in-stock products and recounts products and pages
covers: AC2: lists only products with at least one unit in stock
AC2: product count and pages count only those
AC2: the address bar keeps the choice
items.reason: AC2 is the core shopper journey: one click must change the list, the product count and the number of pages, and record the choice in the URL. Checking the counts in the browser proves the WebApp passes the filter to the API (a WebApp that forgot it would still show 101).

items.title: A reload or a shared link with inStock=true shows the same filtered list
covers: AC2: a reload or a shared link shows the same list
items.reason: AC2 requires the choice to live in the URL so that a reload or a link opened by someone else reproduces it. The page reads it from the query string on first render, which only a fresh navigation in a real browser exercises.

items.title: "In stock only" with a brand and a type applies all three
covers: AC3: 'In stock only' with a brand and a type, all apply at once
items.reason: AC3 from the shopper's side: toggling a brand or type must keep `inStock` in the URL and vice versa, or one filter silently drops another. Daybird + Ski/boarding has 4 products, 2 out of stock, so the result is small and exact.

items.title: Paging keeps the type and "In stock only" filters
covers: AC3: paging keeps every filter
AC2: pages count only in-stock products
items.reason: AC3 says paging keeps every filter; a pager link built without `inStock` would show out-of-stock products on page 2 and a different total. Ski/boarding with "In stock only" has 14 products, so there are exactly two pages.

items.title: Sort order applies together with "In stock only" and survives paging
covers: AC3: 'In stock only' with a sort order, all apply at once
AC3: paging keeps the sort order
items.reason: AC3 names the sort order explicitly. The sort runs in the browser (`catalog-sort.js`) on the cards the filtered page renders, so only e2e shows that the two work together and that the chosen sort is still applied after moving to page 2.

items.title: "Clear all filters" in the filter panel turns "In stock only" off
covers: AC4: 'Clear all filters' turns 'In stock only' off with the other filters
items.reason: AC4: the reset link must drop `inStock` together with brand and type; a reset that kept it would leave the shopper with a hidden filter and 90 products instead of 101.

items.title: "Clear all filters" in the empty state turns "In stock only" off
covers: AC2: only in-stock products are listed (none here)
AC4: 'Clear all filters' turns 'In stock only' off
items.reason: "In stock only" can empty a selection that has products (Daybird Bags holds only the out-of-stock Trailblaze hiking backpack). The catalog then shows its own "Clear all filters" button, a second reset path (`ResetFiltersUri` in `Catalog.razor`) that AC4 also covers; if it kept `inStock`, the shopper would stay stuck on a filtered list.

items.title: Turning "In stock only" off again lists every product
covers: AC1: 'In stock only' is an option the shopper can switch
AC2: the address bar keeps the choice
items.reason: An option that can be switched on must be switchable off without "Clear all filters", or the shopper loses other filters to undo it. Kept separate from TC-INSTK-1-15 because it checks that only `inStock` is removed while the brand stays.

subject: INSTK-1
reason: Council (testPlan, blockOn any, pass 9/10): not passed; opus 8/10, sol 9/10; 1 finding(s) stand, 1 note(s).

items.reason: Add an e2e case with a selected brand, inStock=true and enough matching seeded products for two pages. Navigate to page 2 and assert that brand and inStock remain in the URL, the filters remain active, and the exact products and count match the seeded selection.

The functional preconditions say only 'the Catalog functional fixture' and claim existing tests touch only items 1 and 2. In fact CatalogApiTests (IClassFixture<CatalogApiFixture>, one shared database) deletes items 5 and 6 (DeleteCatalogItem), adds items 10015 and 10016 with stock 100 (AddCatalogItem, never removed) and adds then deletes 99901/99902. TC-05 expects item 5 present with stock 0 and count 101; TC-01 expects count 90; TC-06/07 expect 101 including item 5. These fail depending on order if the cases go into CatalogApiTests. The plan must say the INSTK-1 functional cases run in their own test class with its own CatalogApiFixture (fresh seed), or exclude the changed rows and recompute the numbers.

subject: INSTK-1
reason: Council (testPlan, blockOn any, pass 9/10): passed; opus 9/10, sol 10/10; 0 finding(s) stand, 2 note(s).

items.reason: 'Items in data are ordered by name, as before the change' does not say which comparison: GetAllItems orders in Postgres (OrderBy(c => c.Name), container default collation), so an ordinal client-side check would fail on e.g. 'Trailblaze hiking backpack' vs 'Trailblaze Steel-Blue Hiking Shoes'. Assert instead that the id sequence equals the v1 response for the same PageSize/PageIndex (v1 is unchanged), or state the collation.

Rationale says 'No brand in the INSTK-1 stock set has more than 9 in-stock products'; WildRunner and Raptor Elite each have 11 in stock there (none out of stock). The real reason for the extra scenario is that no brand has both an out-of-stock item and more than 9 in-stock items. The case itself is correct; minor wording fix only.

subject: implementer
reason: Clicking "In stock only" in the WebApp puts inStock=True (capital T) in the address bar instead of inStock=true.

items.expected: After clicking "In stock only" on /, the address bar contains inStock=true
items.actual: The address bar is http://localhost:29080/?inStock=True; filtering, the 90-product count and the 10 pages are correct
items.reason: NavigationManager.GetUriWithQueryParameters formats the boxed bool true as "True", so the URL does not match the inStock=true the verified case, the API parameter, CatalogService and the implementation notes all use. The same click and check in TC-INSTK-1-12 and TC-INSTK-1-18 fail the same way. Passing the string "true" would fix it.
